issues.what: The cursor silhouette covers the ball in both close-ups, and the first shot fills the frame with a short stretch of lane without showing where the ball is headed. The launch and handoff to the playfield are harder to follow than the wide setup.
issues.fix: Keep the ball clear of the cursor once it moves, and frame enough of the lane to show its exit before cutting to the playfield.

issues.where: 1:32.53–1:41.67, overhead view of the Entry-Level playfield
issues.what: The tiny changing commentary sits right against the bottom edge and is partly cropped in some framings. It competes with following the ball instead of reading as a distinct response to a hit.
issues.fix: Keep the hit feedback inside a consistent safe area at a readable size, and hold each response long enough to register after the contact.

issues.where: 1:55.93–2:04.30, lower-center pill and moving Submit button
issues.what: After the labeled Submit button moves to the right, a second dark button-shaped pill remains at the original position and gets attention rays. The placeholder staging does not clearly distinguish which object the cursor is meant to chase.
issues.fix: Make the shape left behind read as a spent outline or impact mark, and give the labeled moving button the strongest action cue.

issues.what: Several successive samples linger on the same full-form composition as the first name grows by a few letters at a time. The keyboard obstacle is established well before the sequence reaches its next escalation.
issues.fix: Hold the first clear obstruction, compress the repeated keystrokes, and keep a short payoff on the completed field before the keyboard changes for the last name.

issues.what: The same chase composition continues through multiple similarly staged interruptions. The timer, cookie prompt, errors and leave dialog get almost equal emphasis, so the sequence lacks a clear escalation toward the button breaking apart.
issues.fix: Give one interruption a clean setup and payoff, compress the others into a quicker escalation, then leave a clear beat for the final click.
